tests.weakness: Quantity is never validated server-side: negative quantities produce a negative order total that is 'paid' as store credit, and a quantity of 1e9 is accepted against 10 units of stock.
Checkout trusts client-supplied unit_price, shipping and grand total from hidden form fields, so a 500.00 item is purchased end-to-end for 0.01.
The order 'integrity' HMAC uses a hardcoded key leaked in client JS and is computed over the order id only, so a paid order's line items and total can be rewritten with a valid signature.

Single-use coupon redemption is check-then-act with no row lock: two genuinely parallel requests both redeem ONCE50 (uses=2, max_uses=1). The flash-sale window is evaluated against a client-supplied purchase_time, so an expired sale price is still accepted.
The 'one per customer' WELCOME5 promo is enforced with a session flag, not per account: the same account redeems it again from a fresh session/cookie jar.
Order confirmation never checks payment state, and fulfilment ships unpaid orders (and even order ids that do not exist), so mandatory workflow steps can be skipped or reordered.
Gift-card redemption has no rate limiting, lockout or anomaly detection: a bounded 300-request sweep of the GC-XXXX space finds GC-1234 and credits the attacker's balance.

Upload validation is a client-side accept attribute plus a lowercase .exe/.sh blacklist; a PHP payload named probe.php.jpg with Content-Type image/jpeg is stored and EXECUTED by the media host (AddHandler), and .html is served as text/html.

The bulk-import pipeline joins raw zip entry names onto the target dir (zip-slip): a ../../pwned.php entry escapes the import directory into the web root and executes. A script-bearing SVG is accepted and served inline as image/svg+xml.

The payment intent amount is client-overridable (a 500.00 order is settled with a 0.01 intent), the 'succeeded' callback is unauthenticated and never reconciled (even for a nonexistent intent), and a negative refund extracts credit.

Cart-add reserves stock with expires_at=NULL and no per-user cap; the expiry sweep never releases anything. An attacker holds all 3 units of the Limited Sneaker without paying and a legitimate buyer's checkout is rejected with 409.
